abstract: We present MindBridge, a clinician-informed, multilingual, multimodal cognitive monitoring tool combining participant-controlled interviews with explainable reports. Reports link lexical diversity and pause patterns to speech or text evidence and disclose data quality and missingness. In a formative study of typed interaction with 10 adults (seven aged 18-59; three aged 60 or older), follow-ups prompted elaboration but sometimes introduced assumptions requiring correction. Nine participants ranked interpretation-first reports highest; all identified score-only reports as most likely to encourage fixation and overreaction. On a fixed DementiaBank manifest, the best configuration achieved 70.3% zero-shot accuracy on valid predictions versus a 56.0% majority-class baseline on the full manifest. Some configurations predicted only one category; tests with generated samples revealed different error patterns across input types and languages. MindBridge makes evidence collection, analysis, and interpretation inspectable, linking participant control to the scope and limits of monitoring results.

oneSentenceThesis: MindBridge 用有界自适应访谈与先解释后分数的报告连接证据采集与解释，10 人打字研究中 9 人偏好解释优先而固定录音最佳配置达 70.3% 准确率，代价是追问仍引入假设且语音分级与跨语言误差显示平均准确率掩盖系统性失效。
originalTitle: MindBridge: A Multilingual and Multimodal Tool for Interactive Cognitive Monitoring
